subject: Clarify: Chat Completions vs Responses billing units and baseline rate card
messages:
From: Alex Bolton <alex.bolton@streamlinehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@streamlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Quick question — Chat Completions vs Responses billing units

Hi Stephanie,

Hope you’re well. We’re reviewing Redwood’s public docs and preparing a rate-card request for our infra and procurement teams. Two quick questions we need clarified before we move forward:

1) The docs reference Chat Completions, Responses, and legacy Completions endpoints. For billing, are these charged on the same "per-token" basis (input + output tokens), or are there differences in unit definitions (e.g., requests/activations vs tokens)?

2) If we have historical usage on the legacy Completions endpoint, what’s the conversion to Responses tokens so we can estimate monthly spend? Any rounding/minimums we should know about?

We’d appreciate a simple baseline rate card (model tiers + per-1k token rates) and any notes about discounts for committed spend tiers. If helpful, I can share our monthly token footprint.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Bolton
Director of Platform Engineering
Streamline Health

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Bolton <alex.bolton@streamlinehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question — Chat Completions vs Responses billing units

Alex — thanks for the clear questions. I’ll keep this high level and attach a short rate card (Q3) for baseline numbers. Short answers below, followed by a couple of practical examples.

TL;DR:
- All three endpoints ultimately bill on token consumption (input + output), but the newer Responses API consolidates features and slightly simplifies unit accounting.
- Legacy Completions map 1:1 to Responses token units for billing purposes; you can treat prompt+completion tokens as equivalent to input+output in Responses.
- We charge per 1k tokens; rounding is per-token (no 100-token buckets), and we prorate streaming output by tokens generated.

Baseline (hosted API, list prices — see attached rate card for full model tier breakdown):
- Responses / Chat-completion comparable model (small tier) — $0.005 per 1k tokens
- Responses / Chat-completion comparable model (medium tier) — $0.015 per 1k tokens
- Responses / Chat-completion comparable model (large/LLM-tier) — $0.06 per 1k tokens

Notes and examples:
- Chat Completions: historically used by chat SDKs. Billing = input tokens (user messages + system prompts) + output tokens (generated content).
- Responses: our newer unified endpoint; conceptually the same billing but the SDK adds features (structured output, tool-calls). No separate per-request "activation" fee; everything is token-driven.
- Legacy Completions: treated as equivalent token units to Responses. If you reported 1,200,000 prompt+completion tokens last month on legacy, estimate ~1,200,000 tokens billed under Responses.
- Rounding & minimums: we bill at 1-token granularity and report usage to the nearest token; there’s no hidden minimum per-request. Enterprise contracts can include committed-spend floors for discounted tiers.

If you can share a rough monthly token profile (average prompt length, avg output length, number of requests/day), I can run a quick spend estimate. Otherwise, I’ll follow up with a short spreadsheet mapping legacy usage to Responses units.

Attaching: Redwood_Rate_Card_Q3_2025.pdf and a comparison CSV. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if you prefer.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Bolton <alex.bolton@streamlinehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question — Chat Completions vs Responses billing units

Thanks, Stephanie — that helps a lot. Couple follow-ups:

- Can you confirm that model tier pricing (small/medium/large) applies identically to Chat Completions and Responses for the same model family?
- For committed discounts, what are the typical breakpoints (monthly commit) and discount magnitude (ballpark)? Procurement is asking for ranges so they can evaluate options.
- Is there any separate metering for streaming vs non-streaming calls (we have a small fraction of real-time streams)?

If it’s easier, feel free to mark up the attached CSV with estimated monthly costs based on our conservative profile (I’ll reply with that shortly).

—Alex

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick question — Chat Completions vs Responses billing units

Markus / Marissa — looping you in for discount guidance. Streamline Health (DL-2025-STRM-018) is evaluating hosted API; they asked for baseline numbers and committed-discount ranges. They look like mid-market healthcare SaaS — potential to expand to Dedicated in future.

Key asks from procurement: typical monthly commit tiers and ballpark discount percentages. Also confirm streaming has no separate meter.

Proposed quick guidance:
- Commit $5k/mo — 10% discount off list
- Commit $20k/mo — 18% discount off list
- Commit $75k/mo — 30% discount + longer SLA options

Approve to propose these ranges? I’ll then share a marked-up rate card and attach a doc for procurement.

Thanks,
Stephanie

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Looks good to me. Approve the proposed tiers as internal guidance; we can tighten percentages in final commercial terms depending on term length and strategic fit. Streaming is token-metered (no separate meter).

Markus
